trend200.label: 200-day trend
trend200.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
trend200.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

mom12.label: 12-month momentum
mom12.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
mom12.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

snapback.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
snapback.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
snapback.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

vix_high.label: India VIX above 25
vix_high.why: A fear reading this high has marked the later stages of sell-offs more often than the start of them.
vix_high.rule: +1 when India VIX closes at or above 25.

dollar20.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
dollar20.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
dollar20.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

real_yield.label: US real yield shift (60 sessions)
real_yield.why: Gold pays nothing, so it competes with the inflation-protected Treasury yield. Rising real yields make gold dearer to hold.
real_yield.rule: -1 for metals when the 10-year TIPS yield rose 25 bp or more over 60 sessions, +1 when it fell 25 bp or more.

fed_gap.label: Fed gap (2-year minus Fed rate)
fed_gap.why: The 2-year yield runs ahead of the Fed. When it sits well above the Fed rate, hikes are expected: good for the dollar, bad for gold and crypto.
fed_gap.rule: Hikes priced when the gap is +50 bp or more; cuts priced at -50 bp or less.

crowding.label: Futures crowding (CFTC, 3-year range)
crowding.why: When speculative funds are the most long they have been in 3 years, there is no one left to buy and a surprise unwinds fast; the most short is the mirror. The same index as the International positioning cards.
crowding.rule: +1 when the crowding index is 10 or less (most short), -1 at 90 or more (most long).

rate_shock.label: US 2-year yield jump (60 sessions)
rate_shock.why: A fast rise in US short rates pulls foreign money out of Indian stocks and lifts the dollar.
rate_shock.rule: -1 for Indian indexes when the US 2-year rose 50 bp or more in 60 sessions, +1 when it fell 50 bp or more.

drawdown20.label: Bear market (20% below 1-year high)
drawdown20.why: An index 20% or more below its 1-year high has, over the following 3 to 12 months, usually recovered part of the fall. Meant for long holds only.
drawdown20.rule: +1 when the close is 20% or more below its 252-session high.

markets.label: Bank Nifty

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: India VIX above 25
signals.why: A fear reading this high has marked the later stages of sell-offs more often than the start of them.
signals.rule: +1 when India VIX closes at or above 25.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

signals.label: US 2-year yield jump (60 sessions)
signals.why: A fast rise in US short rates pulls foreign money out of Indian stocks and lifts the dollar.
signals.rule: -1 for Indian indexes when the US 2-year rose 50 bp or more in 60 sessions, +1 when it fell 50 bp or more.

signals.label: Bear market (20% below 1-year high)
signals.why: An index 20% or more below its 1-year high has, over the following 3 to 12 months, usually recovered part of the fall. Meant for long holds only.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is 20% or more below its 252-session high.

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 56,823.88 (-9.9% from here).
Snap-back fades once the 20-session move is back inside its usual range.
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.

markets.label: Gold

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

signals.label: US real yield shift (60 sessions)
signals.why: Gold pays nothing, so it competes with the inflation-protected Treasury yield. Rising real yields make gold dearer to hold.
signals.rule: -1 for metals when the 10-year TIPS yield rose 25 bp or more over 60 sessions, +1 when it fell 25 bp or more.

signals.label: Fed gap (2-year minus Fed rate)
signals.why: The 2-year yield runs ahead of the Fed. When it sits well above the Fed rate, hikes are expected: good for the dollar, bad for gold and crypto.
signals.rule: Hikes priced when the gap is +50 bp or more; cuts priced at -50 bp or less.

signals.label: Futures crowding (CFTC, 3-year range)
signals.why: When speculative funds are the most long they have been in 3 years, there is no one left to buy and a surprise unwinds fast; the most short is the mirror. The same index as the International positioning cards.
signals.rule: +1 when the crowding index is 10 or less (most short), -1 at 90 or more (most long).

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 4,415.68 (+21.3% from here).
Snap-back fades once the 20-session move is back inside its usual range.
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.
Fed gap signal ends when the 2-year minus Fed rate is back inside +/-50 bp.

rows.note: Costs about 0.5% a year. No margin calls, no roll, nothing expires. The slow, safe way to hold a year-long view.

rows.vehicle: MCX futures, rolled (about 4.0x on the slice)
rows.note: Measured roll cost +9.7% a year (median since 2025-08-18, last +9.9%): that much of the move is paid away each year just to stay in. Daily mark-to-market: the bad path needs about Rs 47,311 of cash on hand. Margin 11% means full leverage would be 9x; the slice uses less so a 12% fall does not wipe it.

Loss fixed to the premium, but a year of near-month options means about 12 rolls, each paying time value; if the move comes late, the early premiums are gone. Only for the part of the view you expect soon.

longView.wrong: If instead the market falls 12% (its 1-year 5th-percentile move), the ETF loses that much of the slice; the rolled futures lose it times the leverage, plus a year of roll cost; the rolled options lose the premiums paid.

markets.label: Silver

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

signals.label: US real yield shift (60 sessions)
signals.why: Gold pays nothing, so it competes with the inflation-protected Treasury yield. Rising real yields make gold dearer to hold.
signals.rule: -1 for metals when the 10-year TIPS yield rose 25 bp or more over 60 sessions, +1 when it fell 25 bp or more.

signals.label: Fed gap (2-year minus Fed rate)
signals.why: The 2-year yield runs ahead of the Fed. When it sits well above the Fed rate, hikes are expected: good for the dollar, bad for gold and crypto.
signals.rule: Hikes priced when the gap is +50 bp or more; cuts priced at -50 bp or less.

signals.label: Futures crowding (CFTC, 3-year range)
signals.why: When speculative funds are the most long they have been in 3 years, there is no one left to buy and a surprise unwinds fast; the most short is the mirror. The same index as the International positioning cards.
signals.rule: +1 when the crowding index is 10 or less (most short), -1 at 90 or more (most long).

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 66.73 (+54.6% from here).
Snap-back fades once the 20-session move is back inside its usual range.
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.
Fed gap signal ends when the 2-year minus Fed rate is back inside +/-50 bp.

rows.note: Costs about 0.5% a year. No margin calls, no roll, nothing expires. The slow, safe way to hold a year-long view.

rows.vehicle: MCX futures, rolled (about 2.4x on the slice)
rows.note: Measured roll cost +11.5% a year (median since 2025-12-16, last +9.5%): that much of the move is paid away each year just to stay in. Daily mark-to-market: the bad path needs about Rs 66,667 of cash on hand. Margin 20% means full leverage would be 5x; the slice uses less so a 27% fall does not wipe it.

Loss fixed to the premium, but a year of near-month options means about 12 rolls, each paying time value; if the move comes late, the early premiums are gone. Only for the part of the view you expect soon.

longView.wrong: If instead the market falls 27% (its 1-year 5th-percentile move), the ETF loses that much of the slice; the rolled futures lose it times the leverage, plus a year of roll cost; the rolled options lose the premiums paid.

markets.label: Copper

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

signals.label: Futures crowding (CFTC, 3-year range)
signals.why: When speculative funds are the most long they have been in 3 years, there is no one left to buy and a surprise unwinds fast; the most short is the mirror. The same index as the International positioning cards.
signals.rule: +1 when the crowding index is 10 or less (most short), -1 at 90 or more (most long).

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 6.21 (+12.6% from here).
Snap-back fades once the 20-session move is back inside its usual range.
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.

markets.label: WTI crude

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

signals.label: Futures crowding (CFTC, 3-year range)
signals.why: When speculative funds are the most long they have been in 3 years, there is no one left to buy and a surprise unwinds fast; the most short is the mirror. The same index as the International positioning cards.
signals.rule: +1 when the crowding index is 10 or less (most short), -1 at 90 or more (most long).

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 88.66 (+6.7% from here).
Snap-back fades once the 20-session move is back inside its usual range.
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.

rows.note: Costs little; no margin calls, no roll.

rows.vehicle: MCX futures, rolled (about 1.4x on the slice)
rows.note: Measured roll cost -19.3% a year (median since 2026-03-20, last -10.8%): that much of the move is paid away each year just to stay in. Daily mark-to-market: the bad path needs about Rs 66,667 of cash on hand. Margin 31% means full leverage would be 3x; the slice uses less so a 48% fall does not wipe it.

Loss fixed to the premium, but a year of near-month options means about 12 rolls, each paying time value; if the move comes late, the early premiums are gone. Only for the part of the view you expect soon.

longView.wrong: If instead the market falls 48% (its 1-year 5th-percentile move), the ETF loses that much of the slice; the rolled futures lose it times the leverage, plus a year of roll cost; the rolled options lose the premiums paid.

markets.label: Brent crude

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 95.08 (-0.4% from here).
Snap-back fades once the 20-session move is back inside its usual range.
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.

markets.label: Natural gas

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 2.97 (-15.0% from here).

markets.label: Wheat

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 630.02 (+11.2% from here).
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.

markets.label: Cotton

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 76.65 (-5.5% from here).
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.

markets.label: US dollar index

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Fed gap (2-year minus Fed rate)
signals.why: The 2-year yield runs ahead of the Fed. When it sits well above the Fed rate, hikes are expected: good for the dollar, bad for gold and crypto.
signals.rule: Hikes priced when the gap is +50 bp or more; cuts priced at -50 bp or less.

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 100.15 (-3.7% from here).
Fed gap signal ends when the 2-year minus Fed rate is back inside +/-50 bp.

markets.label: USD/INR

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 94.04 (+1.7% from here).
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.

markets.label: Bitcoin

signals.label: 200-day trend
signals.why: Price above its 200-day average: the market is in an uptrend and trends persist (time-series momentum). Below: downtrend.
signals.rule: +1 when the close is above the 200-day average, -1 below it.

signals.label: 12-month momentum
signals.why: Return over the past 12 months, skipping the latest month: the classic momentum measure used by trend funds. Meant for 1 to 12 month holds.
signals.rule: +1 when the 12-month return (ending a month ago) is positive, -1 when negative.

signals.label: Snap-back after an extreme move
signals.why: A 20-session move in the worst 5% of this market's own history is usually forced selling: funds hitting risk limits, margin calls, stops. When they are done there is no one left to sell, so the next weeks lean the other way. The mirror holds for the best 5%.
signals.rule: +1 when the 20-session return is in the bottom 5% of all its past readings, -1 in the top 5%.

signals.label: Dollar direction (20 sessions)
signals.why: A rising dollar pulls money out of dollar-priced commodities and emerging markets; a falling one sends it back. The International radar measures this link.
signals.rule: Dollar index up more than 1.5% in 20 sessions is a rising dollar; down more than 1.5% is a falling one. The market's own sign decides which is bullish.

signals.label: Fed gap (2-year minus Fed rate)
signals.why: The 2-year yield runs ahead of the Fed. When it sits well above the Fed rate, hikes are expected: good for the dollar, bad for gold and crypto.
signals.rule: Hikes priced when the gap is +50 bp or more; cuts priced at -50 bp or less.

signals.label: Futures crowding (CFTC, 3-year range)
signals.why: When speculative funds are the most long they have been in 3 years, there is no one left to buy and a surprise unwinds fast; the most short is the mirror. The same index as the International positioning cards.
signals.rule: +1 when the crowding index is 10 or less (most short), -1 at 90 or more (most long).

cancels: 200-day trend flips at 71,974.04 (+20.2% from here).
Dollar signal ends when its 20-session change is back inside +/-1.5%.
Crowding ends when the index returns inside 10 to 90.
Fed gap signal ends when the 2-year minus Fed rate is back inside +/-50 bp.
